rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.says: PALETTES.md, the hub page on how any app gets reskinned (colour roles, hard floors, coupling, four palette families, measurement traps), is enforced by palette-check.mjs, which exits non-zero when it fails.

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: Canonical HERE — link to it, never fork it.
rules.says: PALETTES.md is canonical in the hub, so any other repository links to it and never keeps a forked copy.
rules.live_quote: Canonical here in the hub, like [`DOCTRINE.md`](DOCTRINE.md) and [`LESSONS.md`](LESSONS.md). **Never fork this into another repo — link to it.**

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: `LESSONS.md` **in this hub** — [cross-app lessons](LESSONS.md): what has actually gone wrong anywhere, with the numbers, so it does not go wrong again somewhere else. Read it with this doctrine at the start of every session
rules.says: The hub's LESSONS.md holds cross-app lessons (what actually went wrong anywhere, with the numbers), and a session reads it together with the doctrine at the start of every session.
rules.live_quote: `DOCTRINE.md` is canonical here, and so is [`LESSONS.md`](LESSONS.md) — the cross-app record of what has actually gone wrong, with the numbers
rules.missing: That a session reads LESSONS.md with the doctrine at the start of every session. CLAUDE.md:31 says the opposite: 'No session loads it; search it when a question is about history.'

rules.heading: LESSONS.md in this hub
rules.quote: what has actually gone wrong anywhere, with the numbers, so it does not go wrong again somewhere else.
rules.says: A lesson in the hub's LESSONS.md records what actually went wrong, in any app, with the numbers, so the same failure is not repeated in another app.
rules.live_quote: the cross-app record of what has actually gone wrong, with the numbers

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: and APPEND to it whenever a session learns something that would have saved time in a different app.
rules.says: A session appends to the hub's LESSONS.md whenever it learns something that would have saved time in a different app.
rules.live_quote: Append to LESSONS.md from any app's session whenever something is learned that would have saved time elsewhere; never fork it into another repo.

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: **It is ENFORCED, not merely read** . Every lesson declares `GATE`, `CHECKLIST` or `JUDGEMENT`, and [`lessons-check.mjs`](lessons-check.mjs) FAILS on a lesson that declares nothing or cites a gate that does not exist.
rules.says: Every lesson in LESSONS.md must declare GATE, CHECKLIST or JUDGEMENT and any gate it cites must exist, otherwise lessons-check.mjs fails.
rules.live_quote: [`lessons-check.mjs`](lessons-check.mjs) — every lesson in LESSONS.md declares `GATE`, `CHECKLIST` or `JUDGEMENT`, and a cited gate that does not exist FAILS.

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.says: A session runs node lessons-check.mjs --checklist before any handoff.
rules.live_quote: `--checklist` prints the steps no script can perform; run it before any handoff.

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: Doctrine says what to do; Lessons says what went wrong and what it cost.
rules.says: Division of roles to act on: the doctrine says what to do, while LESSONS.md records what went wrong and what it cost.
rules.live_quote: The doctrine says what to do; the lessons say what it cost to find out;

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: A repo may keep its own `LESSONS.md` for stack-contract detail (build/deploy/vendor conventions specific to that codebase) — that is a different, repo-local document.
rules.says: A repository may keep its own LESSONS.md for stack-contract detail specific to that codebase (build, deploy, vendor conventions), and it is a different, repo-local document from the hub's cross-app LESSONS.md.

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: **SAYING A LESSON OUT LOUD IS NOT RECORDING IT, AND THE ONES ABOUT YOUR OWN CONDUCT ARE THE ONES THAT GET SAID.** Lessons about the CODE get written without being asked
rules.says: Saying a lesson in a reply is not recording it, because a reply ends with the session and the next session starts from the files, so lessons about how the session itself worked must be written to a file and not only narrated.

rules.heading: LESSONS.md in this hub
rules.quote: Lessons about the CODE get written without being asked — a defect is found, the file gets a section, the number goes in.
rules.says: When a session finds a defect in the code, it writes a section about it into the lessons file and puts the number in, without waiting to be asked.

rules.heading: LESSONS.md in this hub
rules.quote: A session noticed it had been spawning a wait-shell per status check, described the better approach in chat, and wrote no rule
rules.says: A session does not spawn a wait-shell for each status check, and when it notices a better approach to its own working method it writes the rule into the file rather than describing it in chat.

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: **So: a lesson about to go into a reply goes into the file FIRST, and the reply says where it went.**
rules.says: A lesson that is about to go into a reply is written into the lessons file first, and the reply then says where it went; if it is not worth writing down it is not worth saying.

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: This binds hardest on a session's own behaviour, where the pull to narrate rather than record is strongest
rules.says: The write-it-to-the-file-first rule binds hardest on lessons about the session's own behaviour, where the pull to narrate (and apologise) rather than record is strongest, since an apology feels discharged by being spoken.

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: **AND THE MECHANISM IS THE CLOSING REFLECTION, WHICH IS WHY THIS KEEPS HAPPENING.** Replies here habitually end with a reflective note
rules.says: Standing fact a session relies on: the habitual reflective closing note of a reply (a 'worth naming', 'one thing I'd flag about my own conduct') generates lessons with no write step attached and delivers them as prose that is discarded, which explains the repeated failure to record conduct lessons.

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: **So the closer is a trigger, not a flourish.** If a reply is about to end with a reflection on how the session worked, that reflection is a lesson candidate and there are exactly two honest endings
rules.says: When a reply is about to end with a reflection on how the session worked, treat it as a lesson candidate with exactly two allowed outcomes: it goes in the file and the reply names where, or it is neither written nor said.

rules.heading: ## 12. Source-of-truth files (naming convention)
rules.quote: A closing observation that is not worth a paragraph in a file is not worth a paragraph in a reply
rules.says: A closing observation not worth a paragraph in a file is not worth one in a reply, and a session does not fill the closing slot with manufactured self-criticism.
